heading: NEET PG 2026 Answer Key Highlights: NBEMS to issue response sheets, answer key at nbe.edu.in
paragraphs: The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) is expected to upload the NEET PG 2026 answer key and response sheets of candidates by mid-September 2026; however, the board has not issued any official confirmation on the release date yet.

As outlined in the NEET PG 2026 information brochure, NBEMS will release the answer keys and response sheets for NEET PG for the first time, following the Supreme Court’s directions on examination transparency. Indianexpress.com is trying to connect with the officials for more information on the answer key release date, normalisation, and other post-exam related events; a response by the board is expected soon.

Once uploaded online, candidates will be able to check the question IDs, correct answers and their recorded responses through the official website of the board, nbe.edu.in or cdn3.digialm.com. Candidates will be required to enter their login credentials, such as the application number and date of birth (DOB) or password.

The response sheet will allow candidates to compare the answers they marked during the examination with the correct NEET PG 2026 answer key. Candidates can use the answer key and response sheet to calculate their approximate score before the declaration of the result.
According to the schedule uploaded on the official website of NBEMS, the NEET PG 2026 result is scheduled to be declared by September 30.

This year, the NEET PG 2026 was conducted on August 30 in a single shift from 9 am to 12:30 pm. As announced by the board, a total of 2,73,096 candidates had registered for the exam, out of which 2,65,980 candidates appeared. The exam was carried out offline in computer-based examination mode at 1,111 examination centres across 339 cities in the country.

The reduction in the number of questions has also changed the maximum marks in NEET PG 2026. The paper contains 180 questions, with four marks available for every correct response, bringing the maximum score to 720. Incorrect responses attract a one-mark penalty, while unanswered questions do not affect the score.

According to the NEET PG 2026 information bulletin, the validity of the NEET PG 2026 scorecards will be only for the current admission session of 2026-27 for MD / MS / PG diploma courses. Candidates will not be able to carry forward their scores for the next admission session.

NBEMS will also release the score given to candidates for each of the questions as per the marking scheme. Once released online, candidates can access the question ID numbers, the correct answer key to the questions, and responses marked through their applicant login on the official website.

In addition to the NEET PG 2026 answer key, NBEMS will issue the response sheets containing the responses marked by the candidates in the exam. The response sheet will be uploaded by the board on its official website. Candidates will be able to access it by entering their login credentials such as application number and date of birth or password.

As mentioned in the NEET PG 2026 information bulletin, NBEMS, for the first time, will release the answer keys on its official websites, nbe.edu.in, natboard.edu.in or cdn3.digialm.com. Candidates will be able to check the answer keys, once released, after signing in.

NBEMS has announced that every question asked in the NEET PG 2026 question paper will be reviewed by faculty members from the concerned speciality area after the conduct of the entrance examination to re-check the technical correctness of the questions as well as the answer keys. The board has added that, in case any technically incorrect/ambiguous question is found in the post-examination review, candidates will be given full marks for such questions, regardless of whether candidates have attempted them or not.

NBEMS had provided a chance for candidates to challenge the NEET PG 2026 questions for technical errors, if any, with supporting literature, within two calendar days after the conduct of the examination, as mentioned in the official exam information bulletin. The board has also clarified that no claims made beyond two days of the exam date would be entertained under any circumstances.
Candidates will not get the opportunity to apply for re-evaluation, re-checking, or re-totalling of the responses marked by them in NEET PG 2026, according to the examination authority, i.e. NBEMS

The NEET PG 2026 scorecards will only be available on the official website for six months from the date of declaration of the result. This implies that candidates will not be able to download their scorecards after six months from the result declaration date. Additionally, NBEMS has informed candidates in the information bulletin that any requests to provide scorecards over email or through the communication web portal, or to issue the scorecards after expiry of this window, will be rejected.

The development means the answer key and evaluation process cover an examination cycle that included both the main test and a separately conducted test for affected candidates.

All the candidates who appeared for the NEET PG 2026 received 42 minutes for each of the five sections. Each section consisted of 36 questions. Together, the five sections made up 180 questions and 210 minutes of examination time.

NBEMS announced that 2,63,535 candidates were able to complete the NEET PG 2026 examination smoothly. The overall examination duration of the NEET PG 2026 exam remained same, i.e. three hours and 30 minutes.
